To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ultrasound examination is an important diagnostic tool in the determination of the maximal thickness of malignant melanoma of skin.

the correlation between preoperative ultrasound examination and postoperative histometry of tumour thickness is strong and that ultrasound examination underestimats tumour thickness in the presence of subtumoral remnants or subtumoral infiltration.
high-frequency ultrasound scanners are suitable for the noninvasive determination of the maximal tumour thickness in primary malignant melanoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a method for preoperative determination of tumour size in primary malignant melanomas of the skin.
the question of whether the determination of tumour cell thickness by means of high-resolution ultrasound is a useful diagnostic tool.
the value and limits of preoperative ultrasound examination in malignant melanoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ultrasound is a valuable method of measuring tumour thickness, but that it cannot be used as the only criterion in preoperative planning of the extent of excision of a malignant melanoma.

the maximal tumour thickness can be estimated by means of ultrasound, but that the accuracy of this estimation depends on the quality of the ultrasound examination and on the histopathological characteristics of the individual tumour.
high-frequency ultrasound is a useful and reliable method for determining the thickness of malignant melanoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of modern ultrasound scanners in preoperative staging of malignant melanoma of skin has a great advantage for the patient.

high-resolution ultrasound can be used to measure the tumour thickness of a malignant melanoma preoperatively, provided that the tumour is homogeneous and that the tumour cells are not smaller than the resolution of the ultrasound scanner.

the preoperative ultrasound determination of vertical tumour thickness in malignant melanomas can be used as an aid for the surgeon in planning operative therapy and determining minimal excision margins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of modern high-frequency scanners for preoperative tumour thickness determination of primary malignant melanoma should be considered in all patients with melanoma.
the accuracy of preoperative ultrasound examination depends on the experience of the examiner.
ultrasound examination can be used to plan the extent of the excisional biopsy and to estimate tumour thickness in malignant melanomas.
